fields.body:
# Anthropic — 10-Year Thesis Ledger
> v1.0 · 2026-08-22 · Approved by: Director · status: active
> ⚠ Disclosure of interest: Essays on this site are written with Anthropic's model (Claude).
> This ledger and all essays rely only on official announcements and third-party reports, and apply
> the same evidentiary standard to praise and criticism.

## 10-Year Thesis
An empirical experiment testing the proposition that "intelligence built safely sells at the highest price." We observe whether the premium enterprises
pay for trust is a sustainable moat — whether a toll-style enterprise business can hold up
amid frontier model competition.

## Core Hypotheses
1. **The enterprise toll is real** [Conviction: High]
   Basis: ARR $47B (May) → $65B (end of July), 40% share of enterprise LLM spending (Menlo, #1),
   1,000 customers at $1M+ (doubled in six months), 8 of the Fortune 10, first adjusted operating profit in 2026 2Q.
   Refutation condition: share drops below 30% and price competition eats into margins —
   evidence that it was a commodity, not a toll.
2. **Claude Code = a See's Candies moment** [Conviction: High]
   Basis: 54% of coding-specialized LLM spending — a moat created by a single product. The trajectory from $500M (2025.9)
   to a projected $23.5B contribution (2027.5).
   Refutation condition: half the share is eroded by competing agents, or a sharp fall in coding automation unit prices
   deflates the market itself.
3. **Multicloud neutrality is a structural advantage** [Conviction: Medium]
   Basis: distribution across all clouds — AWS, Google, Azure — plus the SpaceX Colossus compute contract —
   the only frontier lab not tied to any single empire.
   Refutation condition: dependence on a particular cloud exceeds half of revenue and bargaining power reverses.
4. **Regulation and geopolitics are real variables** [Conviction: —]
   Basis: in 2026.6 export controls took Fable/Mythos offline for 3 days → restored after release — a preview of an era in which frontier
   models are treated as national strategic assets. Under observation.

## Relationship to the Buffett Scale
Unlisted (Nasdaq IPO planned for October; S-1 filed; reports that underwriters sized it on a $965B valuation and 2028 revenue of $190–200B).
If it lists, we will consider adding it to the Parallax universe, but the initial
multiple will almost certainly sit in the too-hard zone — this ledger is the only tool for filling in the coupon box.

## Next Observation Points
- IPO schedule and offering terms (expected October) — the first public test of valuation
- 3Q ARR trajectory (the slope after $65B)
- Next model cycle and defense of enterprise share (three-way race with Gemini 4 and the next GPT)
